notes.body:
Whole-body model of omeprazole
PBPK/PD model of omeprazole with its enantiomers S-omeprazole and R-omeprazole, their metabolism in the liver by CYP2C19 and CYP3A4, the renal and biliary excretion of the metabolites, the absorption of the application forms and the inhibition of the gastric proton pumps.
The content of this model has been carefully created in a manual research effort.

body.p: Activity of CYP2C19 relative to the extensive metabolizer (*1/*1): the mean activity of the two alleles of the genotype (*1 1.0, *2 and *3 0 (no function), *17 1.5 (increased function)), i.e. extensive metabolizers 1.0, intermediate metabolizers 0.5 and poor metabolizers 0; multiplied by the factors of inhibiting drugs. Set by the experiments, never fitted.
Activity of CYP3A4 relative to the reference; inhibitors < 1, inducers

ol.li: Set by the experiments, never fitted.

parameter.name: rate of the omeprazole exchange between plasma and liver

body.p: Fast exchange (not fitted): the liver is in equilibrium with its plasma, the uptake does not limit the metabolism.

Apparent Michaelis constant of CYP2C19 for S- and R-omeprazole of the total concentration in the liver: the Km of the high affinity 5-hydroxylation of liver microsomes (2.5-6 µM unbound, Andersson et al. 1993, Br J Clin Pharmacol 36:521) over the unbound fraction of omeprazole (0.05, 95 % bound), about 100 µM. Not fitted: the fits ran the Km to the upper bound of 50 µM with a lower cost (265 vs 270), it is not identifiable above it. The dose dependence of the bioavailability (Andersson1990a: 0.40 at 10 mg, 0.58 at 40 mg) comes from the mechanism-based inactivation of CYP2C19 during the first pass and the saturation of CYP2C19 at the portal concentrations of the larger doses.
Michaelis constant of the CYP3A4 sulfoxidation, high (about 100 µM in vitro): linear at clinical doses. Not fitted.

parameter.name: fraction 5-hydroxyomeprazole of the CYP2C19 metabolism of S-omeprazole

body.p: CYP2C19 converts S-omeprazole mainly to 5-O-desmethylomeprazole; the 5-hydroxyomeprazole from S-omeprazole is 7 % of the one from R-omeprazole (HassanAlin2005 Tab4: AUC 0.11 vs 1.59 µmol*h/l). Not fitted.

parameter.name: fraction 5-hydroxyomeprazole of the CYP3A4 metabolism of R-omeprazole

body.p: CYP3A4 forms 5-hydroxyomeprazole besides the sulfone (the low affinity 5-hydroxylation of liver microsomes, Andersson et al. 1993, Br J Clin Pharmacol 36:521), the route of 5-hydroxyomeprazole in CYP2C19 poor metabolizers: their plasma and urine contain 5-hydroxyomeprazole (Sohn1992: Cmax 46 ng/ml, urine 5.6 % of the dose against 13.5 % of extensive metabolizers; Uno2007: PO AUC 364 vs 656 ng*h/ml). The 5-hydroxyomeprazole comes from R-omeprazole (HassanAlin2005 Tab4), the fraction is fitted.
The value of LI__f_rome_cyp3a4_omeoh is the result of the fit PK_20261020_090631__aa2cf, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: concentration of half-maximal inactivation of CYP2C19

body.p: Apparent inactivation constant of the total liver concentration (in vitro KI of a few µM [Ogilvie2011, Boulenc2012]): the inactivation is saturated at the liver concentrations of a dose. Not fitted: not identifiable together with the inactivation rate; a KI of 0.1 mM (the in vitro KI over the unbound fraction) gave a higher cost (279.6 vs 265-270).
The intrinsic clearance of S-omeprazole is about a third of the one of R-omeprazole [Abelo2000]: S AUC 2.5 fold R after a single oral dose (HassanAlin2005).
The value of LI__CYP2C19_Vmax_some is the result of the fit PK_20261020_090631__aa2cf, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: rate of the 5-hydroxyomeprazole oxidation in the liver

body.p: The 5-hydroxyomeprazole of the liver is released into the plasma (OMEOHEX_k) or oxidized to the secondary metabolites (5-hydroxyomeprazole sulfone, carboxyomeprazole); the fraction released is OMEOHEX_k/(OMEOHEX_k + OMEOHM_k). In the plasma 5-hydroxyomeprazole is excreted by the kidneys.

parameter.name: rate of the metabolite exchange between plasma and liver

body.p: Fast exchange of omeprazole sulfone and the other metabolites between the liver and its plasma (not fitted).

parameter.name: rate of the CYP2C19 metabolism of omeprazole sulfone

body.p: Omeprazole sulfone is hydroxylated by CYP2C19 to 5-hydroxyomeprazole sulfone: half-life 2-2.6 hr in extensive metabolizers [Andersson1990a, HassanAlin2000, Palovaara2003].
The value of LI__OMESUL2C19_k is the result of the fit PK_20261020_090631__aa2cf, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

blockquote.p: 1.0: increased kidney function 1.0: normal kidney function (healthy control) <1.0: decreased kidney function

body.p: Renal function relative to the healthy glomerular filtration rate GFR_base, which is 101 ml/min at 75 kg; a measured creatinine clearance of X ml/min is the renal function X/101.

parameter.name: renal clearance of 5-hydroxyomeprazole relative to the GFR

body.p: The renal clearance of 5-hydroxyomeprazole is OMEOHEX_f times the GFR: above 1 a net secretion. The 5-hydroxyomeprazole of the plasma is excreted in the urine (13.5 % of the dose in extensive metabolizers [Sohn1992]), half-life about 1 hr [Andersson1990a].
The value of KI__OMEOHEX_f is the result of the fit PK_20261020_090631__aa2cf, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: renal clearance of the other metabolites relative to the GFR

body.p: The renal clearance of the secondary metabolites (5-hydroxyomeprazole sulfone, carboxyomeprazole) is OMEOTHEX_f times the GFR; with the biliary excretion it gives 75-78 % of the dose in the urine and 17-19 % in the feces [Regaardh1986, Regaardh1990].
The value of KI__OMEOTHEX_f is the result of the fit PK_20261020_090631__aa2cf, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: enteric-coated form (0 solution or suspension, 1 enteric-coated)

body.p: 1: capsule with enteric-coated pellets, enteric-coated tablet, MUPS tablet, enteric-coated granules; 0: solution or suspension. Set by the experiments from the application form.

parameter.name: unprotected solution (0 buffered or enteric-coated, 1 unprotected)

body.p: 1: a solution or suspension without bicarbonate buffer, which the gastric acid degrades (F_ome_pH); 0: buffered solution or suspension and the enteric-coated forms. Set by the experiments.

parameter.name: rate of the gastric emptying of a solution

body.p: Gastric emptying of a buffered solution: tmax 0.2-0.3 hr [Andersson1990a, Andersson1993, Naesdal1986, Regaardh1990]. Fast, not fitted: the absorption OMEABS_k limits the uptake, the fits spread the rate over 9-60 /hr at the same cost.

parameter.name: rate of the gastric emptying and the release of an enteric-coated form

body.p: The enteric-coated pellets leave the stomach and dissolve in the small intestine, both with this rate (a delayed release): tmax 1.5-2.5 hr [Elkoshi2002, Palovaara2003, Uno2007].
The value of GU__Ka_ec_ome is the result of the fit PK_20261020_090631__aa2cf, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: fed effect on the gastric emptying and dissolution

body.p: A meal slows the gastric emptying of the enteric-coated pellets: tmax +1.5 to +3 hr, Cmax x0.34-0.40 (VazdaSilva2005, high-fat breakfast). Not fitted (one study).

parameter.name: fed effect on the fraction absorbed

body.p: A meal lowers the exposure: AUC x0.62-0.66 at steady state (VazdaSilva2005, high-fat breakfast). Not fitted (one study).
Omeprazole is absorbed completely: the urinary recovery of the radioactivity is the same after IV and oral doses, no unchanged omeprazole in the feces [Regaardh1986, Andersson1993]. Not fitted.
The value of GU__OMEABS_k is the result of the fit PK_20261020_090631__aa2cf, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.
